subject: ADR-188: names at the door -- every selector argument takes a control ADDRESS (#id, @name, or an index stamped with its snapshot), and every control publishes the shortest one that resolves back to it
body: THE COMPLAINT ALL FOUR BLIND OPERATORS MADE. action_btn:N indexes the whole page and renumbers on every structural change; the snapshot publishes a stable id; no tool accepted one, because @control:<name> was resolved by the TASK RUNNER, on the far side of the door the operator speaks through. Every selector argument now takes an address: the index as before, the index stamped with the snapshot it came from (kind:index@v<digest>), the page's own id (#cName), or the page's own name (@working name, @rCov/4, @iList/died#2, @kind=drop_zone) -- ADR-128's grammar unchanged, and '@control:' accepted verbatim. Every control publishes the shortest address that resolves back to itself through the resolver itself; on the four trial pages every control has one and no index is left. observe carries a version digest of the numbering; a stamped index whose version moved is refused and told what is at that index now instead of pressing it. risk_for resolves first -- otherwise every stable address would have read as 'resolves to nothing' and been raised to DESTRUCTIVE -- and does not raise a name that names nothing, while an unresolvable positional selector still is (ADR-141) and a destructive control still is through either spelling. The runner keeps its own find_control and the two are held to each other on every name of three real pages. verify_report 120 -> 136, mutate_report 75 -> 89. No page and no task was edited; the walk drives the same 25,392 commands.
